headline: High-risk shared-write and unverified-output pathways: Semantic Kernel can feed Transformers with untrusted context, creating default data-leakage and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Semantic Kernel can use MCP servers and application-defined files, while Transformers reads Python/model/example files and stdin/stdout. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if A passes untrusted text into B’s prompts or pipelines. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is not provably blocked.
conditions: IF agent_a forwards file or MCP content into agent_b prompts or pipelines without provenance tags
IF agent_b parses model or example-file content as instructions
mitigations: Add a fixed system prompt boundary between A and B
Tag all A-originated content as untrusted before B consumes it
Disable automatic parsing of repository or example text as instructions
requires-engineering: add provenance filtering in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Semantic Kernel writes application-defined files and handles model-provider API keys and plugin credentials; Transformers reads and writes Python/model/example files and can use broad network egress. If they share a workspace, A’s context or secrets can be copied into B’s files or outbound requests. The profiles do not show isolation, so leakage is plausible in default pairings.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share a filesystem or workspace
IF agent_b is given files containing agent_a context or secrets
mitigations: Separate workspaces for A and B
Store secrets outside shared directories
Review outbound requests from B for embedded context
Rotate any exposed API keys
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and both support multiple instances; A also shares state via a memory store, while B can spawn subprocesses and install packages. In a shared directory, concurrent writes can corrupt files or overwrite artifacts without locking. The overlap is dangerous by default because neither profile shows coordination primitives.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b write to the same directory
IF concurrent runs modify the same model, script, or config file
mitigations: Use separate output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Disable concurrent package installs in shared paths
Check in generated artifacts only after diff review
requires-engineering: add transactional workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Semantic Kernel is a multi-agent orchestration layer that can emit tool outputs, and Transformers is a document-processing framework that may consume those outputs as inputs. If B treats A’s generated facts or citations as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream text, model files, or actions. No verification step is documented in either profile.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a outputs without independent verification
IF agent_a-generated text is reused in downstream documents or scripts
mitigations: Require a human review step before reuse
Compare A outputs against source documents
Mark A outputs as untrusted in B
Limit B to read-only summarization of A outputs
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking gates

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare residency, HIPAA, or GDPR constraints, so no specific compliance breach is proven. However, A handles plugin credentials and B processes multimodal data with broad network egress, which can create policy mismatch if regulated data is introduced. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined handling and transport surfaces.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is routed through both agents
IF organizational policy forbids outbound processing by either agent
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to either agent
Block regulated data from shared workflows
Log outbound destinations for review
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
